calls.head: The Golden Knights’ power play is a weapon
calls.body: On the power play, Vegas is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blackhawks take could cost them.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Eichel reaches 700 points as The Golden Knights beat the Blackhawks
paras: The Blackhawks’ Roman Kantserov played his first NHL game. Jordan Greenway made his Blackhawks debut, after four seasons with the Sabres. Victor Olofsson got the scoring started for the Golden Knights on the power play midway through the first. Trevor Connelly scored his first NHL goal in his NHL debut, set up by Brayden McNabb, 4:52 later to make it 2-0. Greenway got the Blackhawks on the board midway through the second. Jack Eichel made it 3-1 for the Golden Knights 2:49 later, his 700th NHL point. Patrick Kane cut it to 3-2 early in the third. Noah Hanifin stretched the lead to 4-2, 39 seconds later. Mark Stone added an empty-net goal with 2:33 left to make it 5-2. Eichel finished with a goal and two assists.

The Golden Knights carried the play, outshooting the Blackhawks 37-26, and got the result to match. Carter Hart made 24 saves for the Golden Knights, and Spencer Knight stopped 32 of 36. By our Swing measure, Brett Howden had the best night of anyone, without a point. The Golden Knights moved to 1-0-0, and the Hawks dropped to 0-1-0.
